TL;DR: achievable with carveouts and dedicated capacity; requires Product & Sales alignment on commercial uplift and operational runbook.

Details:
- Feasibility: For their workload profile (peak 220 rps, median seq len ~80 tokens), hitting P95 <100ms reliably on shared fleets is high risk. We can meet target if we: (a) provision a dedicated GPU pool with reserved capacity sized for their 99th-percentile expected concurrency, (b) enforce strict request-level admission controls (token limits + prioritized traffic), and (c) enable aggressive KV/prefix caching for common prompts.
- Fallbacks: Implement automatic fallback to a slightly lower-capacity model variant (quantized) with detectable quality regression thresholds and a runbook to notify the customer. That preserves availability without violating the P95 objective for their primary requests.
- Monitoring & Instrumentation: Need per-customer latency SLI dashboards, per-route tracing, and synthetic probes from the customer region. SRE will own alerting thresholds and the incident play.
- Cost & Ops: Dedicated pool + 24/7 SLA increases unit cost ~1.9x. We should require either Reserved Capacity contract (6-12m commit) or a premium monthly fee to offset ops burden.

Recommendation: Approve conditional exception if Sales agrees to Reserved Capacity + 30% commercial uplift and accepts a scoped maintenance window (2 hours/week, scheduled outside their trading hours). If Sales prefers not to bill uplift, require canary rollouts and a stricter cap on sustained concurrency.

I can put together a sizing sketch and estimated uplift numbers by EOD tomorrow.

—Marcus
Principal Product Manager, Serving | Redwood Inference

Adding SRE perspective and a lightweight runbook stub:

Operational prerequisites:
- Dedicated pool in us-west-2 with reserved nodes (hot spare of +15% capacity) and prioritized networking.
- Per-tenant QoS at the routing layer to enforce request concurrency caps.
- Synthetic probes (one per-minute) and golden prompts for continuous quality checks.

Incident play (summary):
1) Auto-scale probe triggers → immediate notify on-call SRE + account owner.
2) If latency > target and is noisy neighbor → throttle non-priority tiers and route Arcturus to reserved pool.
3) If reserved pool saturated → invoke fallback variant + open incident bridge; notify Arcturus via agreed alarm channel.

Audit & compliance:
- Daily latency SLI export, 30-day retention in audit logs (can be extended per contract).

Risk notes:
- Maintenance windows: we cannot guarantee zero impact during emergency infra events; carve out emergency maintenance with notification SLA (4 hours notice ideally).
- Cost: Dedicated pool and monitoring are non-trivial; needs committed billing to justify capacity reservation.

I can draft the runbook and attach instrumentation dashboards. If Sales confirms the commercial uplift, SRE can support a pilot within 2 weeks.

—Evelyn
Head of SRE | Redwood Inference
